issues.title: fix(macos): restore VPN DNS after network changes
issues.body:
## Problem

The standalone macOS client writes VPN DNS into `Setup:/Network/Service/<UUID>/DNS` at connection time. When macOS refreshes network configuration and removes or replaces that override, the AWG/WireGuard tunnel can remain connected while applications use DHCP DNS. No DNS-change listener reapplies the VPN settings.

This addresses the DNS-loss case reported in [this comment on #3267](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/issues/3267#issuecomment-6070869518). It does not address the separate gateway/ARP failure in the original report.

## Change

- Subscribe to network-service and DNS keys once per DNS utility lifetime, and repair only while the VPN DNS override is active. Deliver native notifications to the Qt object thread through a serial dispatch queue.
- Reapply the desired DNS only when it differs, including for newly added services. Keep the original backup across repairs and repeated updates.
- Disable repair before restoration, invalidate queued work across reconnects, and retain callback context independently of object lifetime. Cancel the native subscription only at destruction: immediate unsubscribe/resubscribe can fail while asynchronous cancellation is still pending.
- Report registration/read/write failures; distinguish missing keys from read errors and preserve failed restoration backups for retry. Do not recreate removed services.
- Add a standalone macOS QtTest suite that compiles the production DNS class, using an in-memory SystemConfiguration boundary without changing host DNS.

## Validation

On Apple silicon, macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 27.1, Qt 6.11.2:

- Original code reproduced deletion recovery, backup corruption, and failure-reporting regressions before the fix.
- Standalone QtTest suite: **21 passed, 0 failed** (19 scenarios plus initialization/cleanup).
- Same suite passed with **AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer**.
- A read-only native SystemConfiguration probe reproduced `kSCStatusNotifierActive` on the second immediate subscribe/unsubscribe cycle. The follow-up regression models pending cancellation and passes with the lifetime subscription.
- Changed production source and MOC compiled against real SystemConfiguration declarations and the production logger, without test API redirects.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Reproduction commands and coverage: `tests/macosdns/README.md`.

Full application/test configuration was attempted but stopped because Conan is not installed. The existing `QString::fromUtf16(UniChar*)` deprecation warning remains unchanged. No replacement service was installed or restarted; actual configd event delivery and USB/DHCP/sleep/Wi-Fi recovery still need end-to-end validation with a built service. The tests prove recovery/lifecycle logic, not installed-app behavior.

issues.title: [iOS][5.1.0.6] AWG 3.1: connected but no traffic — path-update loop rebinds UDP socket every 2–3 s (works in 5.0.3.0 and AmneziaWG)
issues.body:
## Summary

On iOS, AmneziaVPN **5.1.0.6** connects with an AWG 3.1 profile (handshake confirmed) but no traffic passes. The same profile works in AmneziaVPN **5.0.3.0** and in the **AmneziaWG** app on the same phone.

The tunnel log shows a loop: every 2–3 seconds the network extension handles a "network change", re-applies the endpoint config and rebinds the UDP socket. The interface list does not change between these events.

## Environment

| | Fails | Works | Works |
|---|---|---|---|
| App | AmneziaVPN 5.1.0.6 (`ac175c8a8`) | AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 | AmneziaWG (App Store) |
| Device / iOS | iPhone, iOS 26.6.2 | iPhone, iOS 27.2 | same iPhone as "Fails", iOS 26.6.2 |
| Network | LTE (Russian mobile carrier) | LTE, same carrier | LTE, same carrier |
| Profile | same AWG 3.1 profile (self-hosted server, MTU 1280) | same | same |

- The server is a self-hosted AmneziaWG 3.1 server (amneziawg-go). The client receives the handshake response. On the server, the peer's transfer stops after ~16 KB.
- In 5.1.0.6, a profile to a server inside the same country works. Only the server abroad fails. This matches the socket rebind loop: each rebind creates a new UDP flow, and new flows to foreign addresses can be filtered on mobile networks. This part is a hypothesis.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On iOS 26.6.2, install AmneziaVPN 5.1.0.6.
2. Import an AWG 3.1 profile (`vpn://`).
3. Connect over LTE.
4. Open any website.

**Expected:** traffic passes, as in 5.0.3.0 and in AmneziaWG.
**Actual:** status is "Connected" and the handshake is confirmed, but no websites load.

## Tunnel log (excerpt, redacted)

```
19:34:14 WG: peer(q6Ht…) - Received handshake response
19:34:16 WG: Observed first handshake at last_handshake_time_sec=...
19:34:18 WG: Network change detected with satisfied route and interface order [pdp_ip0, pdp_ip0, utun8]
19:34:18 WG: Path update state: state=started(...) everHadHandshake=true lastNetworkSettingsUpdateAt=2026-11-04 16:34:14 +0000
19:34:18 WG: peer(q6Ht…) - UAPI: Updating endpoint
19:34:18 WG: UAPI: Updating h1..h4 / s1..s4 padding, header protection key
19:34:18 WG: Routine: receive incoming v4 - stopped
19:34:18 WG: UDP bind has been updated
19:34:18 WG: Routine: receive incoming v4 - started
19:34:18 WG: peer(q6Ht…) - Sending keepalive packet
19:34:21 WG: Network change detected ... [pdp_ip0, pdp_ip0, utun8]   <- same block repeats
19:34:24 ...                                                          <- every 2–3 s
19:34:26 ...
19:34:27 ...
19:34:30 ...
```

`lastNetworkSettingsUpdateAt` does not change, so the app does not re-apply network settings. The path updates come from `NWPathMonitor`. On each update, `WireGuardAdapter.didReceivePathUpdate` (amneziawg-apple v3.1.4) calls `wgSetConfig` and `wgBumpSockets`.

## Analysis

- The two app versions use the same `awg-apple/3.1.4` (see `conanfile.py`). The adapter code is the same.
- One build difference: the `awg-apple` recipe in 5.1.0.6 uses `go/1.27.1` (5.0.3.0 uses `go/1.26.0`).
- The AmneziaWG app on the same phone and iOS version works with the same profile (I did not collect its log). The cause is therefore in the 5.1.0.6 build or the app shell, not in iOS alone.
- I did not find what triggers the repeated path updates in 5.1.0.6.

## Possible fix

In `didReceivePathUpdate`, skip `wgSetConfig` and `wgBumpSockets` when the path has not changed. For example, compare `availableInterfaces` and the status with the last path, and ignore the tunnel's own `utun*` interface.

issues.title: fix: find the Linux default gateway when the route table is larger than 8 KB
issues.body:
## Summary

- Parse the netlink route dump in `NetworkUtilities::getGatewayAndIface()` one datagram at a time instead of collecting it into a fixed 8 KB buffer, so the default gateway is found whatever the size of the routing table.
- Request IPv4 routes only and stop at the first main-table route that has a gateway and an interface.
- Zero-initialize the receive timeout and close the netlink socket on every return path.

Fixes #3090. #2997 and #3244 report the same `No default gateway available, skipping exclusion route` symptom.

## Root cause

`getGatewayAndIface()` sends an `RTM_GETROUTE` dump request for all address families, appends every reply datagram to an 8 KB stack buffer and parses it only after `NLMSG_DONE`. The kernel splits the dump into several datagrams. Once the total is over 8 KB (a bit over a hundred routes on a typical desktop), `recv()` truncates a datagram or is called with no space left, `NLMSG_OK` fails and the function returns an empty gateway after `Error in received packet`.

`LinuxRouteMonitor::rtmSendRoute()` needs this gateway for every exclusion (`RTN_THROW`) route, both to add and to delete it. So once the table is that large:

- in the "all except sites" split tunneling mode every added exclusion grows the table, and after roughly the first hundred entries the rest are skipped;
- the exclusions that were added cannot be deleted on disconnect and stay in the main table until reboot;
- on the next connection the table is too large from the start, the exclusion for the server endpoint is skipped as well, and WireGuard packets to the server are routed into the tunnel. A leftover exclusion keeps the previous server working, while switching to another server breaks (#2997).

`struct timeval tv` also had an uninitialized `tv_usec`, so `setsockopt(SO_RCVTIMEO)` could fail with `EDOM` (`Error in received packet: Numerical argument out of domain` in the log), and the socket leaked on every early return.

## Compared with the open PRs

- #3170 raises the buffer to 128 KB and #3231 to 64 KB, but both still collect the whole dump before parsing it, so a larger table (long split tunneling lists, many container networks) fails the same way. Here each datagram is parsed as it arrives, in a 32 KB buffer, the size the kernel caps dump datagrams at, so there is no limit on the table size.
- #3470 reads `/proc/net/route` instead of netlink. This PR keeps netlink and the structure of the function.
- `addExclusionRoute()` calls this function once per exclusion. Stopping at the first route with a gateway, which in practice is in the first datagram, means that with long lists each call no longer re-reads a table that keeps growing.

## Validation

- Built the function into a small test program and ran it against a real routing table with a long split tunneling list (a route dump of about 9 KB): the current code prints `Error in received packet` and returns no gateway, the new code returns the default gateway.
- In a network namespace (`unshare -rn`) with a veth pair, a default route and extra `/32` routes: the current code fails at 1,004 routes, the new code finds the gateway at 20,004 routes.
- Built the Linux client with this change and connected with about 750 split tunneling entries: the endpoint exclusion and all site exclusions are installed, `ip route get <endpoint>` goes through the physical gateway, and the delete requests on disconnect get the gateway too.
- `clang-format` on the changed lines.

- Installed AmneziaVPN: 5.0.3 in Info.plist; installer receipt version 5.0.3.0. The application binary contains both arm64 and x86_64 slices. These versions were read after the reboot, before any updates during this investigation.
- WireGuard.app 1.0.16 (build 27) is also installed.

Evidence:

- The embedded stackshot names the panicked thread dlil_input_utun4.
- AmneziaVPN, AmneziaVPN-service, amneziawg-go, wireguard-go, and WireGuard were all present in the stackshot. A separate WireGuard implementation was therefore running alongside Amnezia's helper; I have not established whether both tunnels were connected or which process owned utun4 at the panic instant.
- Persisted kernel logs show TCP/HTTPS traffic through utun4 shortly before the panic. The inspected pre-panic logs end approximately 17 seconds before the panic; they do not identify the triggering packet or connection.
- memoryPressure is false in the panic snapshot; the panic reports compressor limits and swap space as OK.
- ResetCounter records one reset, zero boot failures, and boot faults wdog,reset_in_1 timeout,dblclick_timeout.

I found one retained panic report for this incident. This is not an on-demand reproducer. SMB traffic, MTU, obfuscation settings, and tunnel ownership at the crash have not been established, so I cannot confirm the original report's proposed packet-length/obfuscation mechanism or attribute this crash specifically to Amnezia.

The matching signature has also been reported in https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/20612 and https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/20864, including reports on the same macOS build. That suggests a shared macOS networking path is worth investigating, without establishing the root cause of this occurrence.

Update check on 2026-11-23: this Mac is offered macOS 26.7.3 and macOS 27.2.1. AmneziaVPN 5.1.1.10 is the latest published release, with a general "Improve stability" note. These updates have not been installed or tested during this investigation. I have not found confirmation that they fix this exact panic.

Is there a known fix or an Apple Feedback reference for this signature? Which additional diagnostics would distinguish the macOS TCP/mbuf path from an interaction between tunnel implementations?
